PullRequest.Title: sessions: show the other Customizations categories with More and Less
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #348173.

The expandable Customizations section below the Sessions list in the Agents window now shows a shorter list by default:

- It shows Overview, Plugins, MCP Servers, Skills, and Instructions, followed by a **More** row that counts the customizations of the other available categories and shows their suggestion badge.
- **More** shows those categories in place, below the ones that are always shown, followed by a **Less** row that hides them again. Neither row appears when no other category is available for the active harness.
- The section remembers per profile whether More or Less was used last.
- Keyboard focus stays in the list: Enter on More moves focus to the first category it shows, and Enter on Less moves it back to More. More and Less expose `aria-expanded`.

The experiment-controlled `sessions.sidebar.customizationsCategories` setting controls this. It defaults to `reduced`; `all` shows every category, as before. It only affects the expandable section at the bottom of the sidebar, not the compact Customizations button or the separate navigation list.

Reviewers should know:

- Keyboard focus restoration is in `AICustomizationShortcutsWidget`. Chromium moves focus out of the focused item before the toolbar update removes it, so the widget decides after the update whether focus left or was removed with the item. It restores focus only when focus is on no element, so it never takes focus from elsewhere.
- `observeVisibleSectionsBadge` accepts an optional set of sections, which More uses for its badge.

### How to test

1. Open the Agents window with AI features enabled and expand the Customizations section below the Sessions list.
2. Check that it shows Overview, Plugins, MCP Servers, Skills, Instructions, and More with a count.
3. Select More: the other categories appear below Instructions, followed by Less. Reload the window: they stay shown.
4. Select Less: they are hidden again. Reload the window: they stay hidden.
5. With the keyboard, move to More and press Enter: focus moves to the first category it shows. Move to Less and press Enter: focus moves back to More.
6. Set `"sessions.sidebar.customizationsCategories": "all"`: every category is shown without More or Less.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/browser/aiCustomizationShortcutsWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewPane.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentsWindowRegistrations.test.ts`: passed (37 passing, 1 pending existing test that needs a focused window).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- Manually verified in a Code OSS Agents window: the steps above, including both window reloads, keyboard focus, and the default when the setting is not set.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore the Agents sidebar with the expandable Customizations pane in reduced mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After workbench restore, the contribution registers fixed-size menu/context state; when the control presentation creates AICustomizationShortcutsWidget, the toolbar renders the header, visible rows, and More. DOM construction and observable reads are on the UI critical path; asynchronous customization-provider enumeration completes later and only updates counts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: fetchAICustomizationItems for the four count-bearing prompt sections and fetchProviderItems for Plugins; concrete providers may enumerate files or invoke an external harness provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one initial request per observed section plus one Plugins request for the active source; repeated reads from the header, More, and individual rows are coalesced by observedSections/pluginCountObserved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the unchanged header already called readTotalCustomizationCount across all items, starting the same effective cold requests; the all-category rows also read these observables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests are started during render but are asynchronous; initial rows render with observable state and later update their counts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CUSTOMIZATION_ITEMS is a static 10-entry list; the reduced More set is at most 6 entries. Effective model-fetch cardinality is one fetch each for Skills, Instructions, Agents, Hooks, plus one provider-items fetch for Plugins, deduplicated by observedSections/pluginCountObserved.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold section fetches can run concurrently by section, exactly as before the PR because the unchanged header observes all sections. More does not create additional requests for an already-observed section. Menu and DOM work is synchronous and fixed-cardinality.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold model, the existing header's readTotalCustomizationCount already marks every count-bearing section and Plugins observed. More repeats getCount/getPluginCount reads but markObserved and markPluginCountObserved coalesce them. Warm reads use the existing derived observables and cached source; no new negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the widget/header call path, More aggregate reads, and model observation guards are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider duration and customization collection size vary by harness/workspace, but request cardinality and coalescing are established and unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new aggregate row performs bounded local iteration and does not increase effective provider/filesystem request cardinality; reduced mode also renders fewer category rows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate More or Less and persist the per-profile expansion preference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command synchronously stores one boolean, the storage/context event changes one context key, MenuWorkbenchToolBar rebuilds a fixed-size action list, then scanDomNode and the existing layout callbacks run. This is the direct interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the show-more boolean in profile storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one keyed boolean store per More/Less activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no More/Less preference or corresponding store before the diff; category visibility was controlled only by existing configuration/context state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The store call occurs in the command path and drives the menu update; it is fixed-size and user initiated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user activation; at most 10 static customization actions are re-evaluated/rendered. Cost does not scale with customization item count because rows show aggregate counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command performs one store operation and one menu update sequence; no burst, queue, or unbounded parallel work is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted boolean is read from the storage service's loaded state on contribution creation and subsequently maintained by its keyed change event. Count observables and provider results remain shared; expanding swaps More for individual rows without refetching observed sections.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action, keyed listener, context key, toolbar menu update, and layout callback are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend-specific persistence latency is not measured, but the payload and frequency are strictly bounded to one boolean per explicit click.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A single bounded preference write per explicit interaction is proportionate to the required persistence and does not fan out with categories or customization count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change active harness, category visibility configuration, or the stored More/Less state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Context/config/storage events recompute availability over the static More set and may trigger one debounced menu rebuild and layout notification. Existing count-model source changes can asynchronously refetch already-observed sections.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch already-observed customization sections after an active harness/source/workspace change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per previously observed static section and one Plugins request; unchanged because the existing header already observes all count-bearing sections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The header and all category rows already observed the same sections, so harness/source changes already scheduled this bounded refetch set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the immediate context/menu update critical path; results update counts later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 6 candidate More entries and 10 total menu entries per event; model refetch cardinality is per already-observed static section, not per customization item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Context updates are synchronous fixed loops; menu change handling is managed by the existing menu service. Model refetches retain pre-existing per-section concurrency and stale-result sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Availability uses current context keys. Model source identity is cached, and observed sections are deduplicated; source changes intentionally refetch the same bounded section set. The PR adds no new cache keys or retained history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: context key dependencies, model observation state, and menu update path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of harness/config changes and provider latency varies, but the changed availability scan is fixed-size and effective request cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Changed work is bounded and external refetch behavior is pre-existing rather than introduced or amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move keyboard focus through the customization rows while a More/Less menu update replaces the focused item
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each focus-in scans the current toolbar rows to remember the focused index; a replacement checks connectivity and, only if browser focus is otherwise lost, focuses the corresponding new row before the existing DOM scan/layout notification.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The scan is bounded by the static toolbar size (at most roughly 11 rows including Overview and More/Less), once per focus-in; replacement work is once per menu update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single microtask handles ambiguous focus-out; menu updates and focus restoration remain serialized on the UI thread with no queued accumulation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only one focused HTMLElement/index pair is retained and cleared when focus leaves or after restoration; no collection or lifetime growth exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event listeners, toolbar cardinality, microtask, and restoration conditions are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact browser focus-event ordering differs by window state, but the bounded loop and single-element retention are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added synchronous DOM work is tiny, fixed-cardinality, and limited to keyboard focus/menu replacement events.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 9 changed files and every diff page. Traced startup/render, count-provider boundaries, More/Less persistence and menu rebuilds, harness/config updates, and focus restoration. No diff-introduced actionable performance regression met the reporting threshold, and the PR did not provide evidence of a shipped regression fix requiring blame attribution.
